posts.content: We had an easy morning and then hiked up to the Pinnacle Overlook.  it was a bit over 8 miles and 1800 feet of elevation gain.  Very pretty hike and cool to see Cumberland Gap from teh overlook.  Hazel got some outside time and Alice stayed under the sofa in her spot.  We are definitley not in our best hiking shape.  We are in the process of deciding what the next things will be.  2 nights here has been nice.  The campground is super sleepy and cheap with our Geezer pass ($12)

posts.title: Day 10 - Cumberland Gap Hiking

posts.content: Made it to Cumberland Gap!!!  Nice windy drive, stopped at the visitor center and looked around.  Found a nice campsite at wilderness road campground.  Hazel very much liked being outside.  In the morning now both ladies go to their spots early.

posts.title: Day 9 - bowling green to Cumberland Gap!

posts.content:
Our rubber roof pulled off.  Not so great.  Fortunately we were on our way to camping world to dump our tanks and about 20 miles from bowling green we heard a giant flapping sound all of a sudden.  We have to drive about 20mph to get to camping world.  Once again they got us more less right in and we waited for a bit for Thor to approve a temporary repair.  

They did a pretty good temp fix, but in reality we should really wait 24 hours to drive it.  We think we will just go to the koa here to limit driving.  

Exciting

posts.title: Day 8 - Exciting

posts.content:
Went to the Bluegrass Museum/Hall of fame.  And then to Monroe grave site.  Bill has a giant headstone- if you can call it that.  It’s almost comical.  

Then we went to his home place.  The road winds on up the hill.  I took a picture of the light in the window in Bills sisters bedroom.  There was a tour guy there.  He was great.  He lived in Charlie’s house about half way down jurusalem Ridge. Dude said the road stopped there for a really long time and you had to walk the rest of the way.  

We drove to Hopkinsville to look for the cemetery Suz’s ancestors are in.  We followed the directions to someone’s house about half a mile off the road.  We couldn’t find it so we left.  And then we stopped at a gas station and did some more research.  Suz could see the cemetery on a satellite view.  We went back and found it.  Pretty cool - we found several and on gravestone that was a lady they didn’t know where she died.  

We then drove to Casey Jones Distillery (our 3rd Harvest Host in a row).  It’s quiet and beautiful here in SW Kentucky.

posts.title: Day 7 - Owensboro to Hopkinsville, KY

posts.content:
We made it!  We are staying at Reid Orchard- 5 generation farm.  They open for Harvest Host guests today!  Good timing.  They are open for tulip gathering and things- and have a cool store with jams and pickled veggies and lots of other stuff.  It’s cool, but kind of sunny.  

Tomorrow we go to the Bluegrass museum!

Went through a bunch of states and saw the big arch in St Louis

posts.content:
Windy! 

Yep the wind arrived early this morning.  Big gusts.  NWS forecast shows the wind gusts a little lower in early afternoon.  

40+mph winds.  Ugg.  We made it though!  To a harvest host- super great folks winery/restaurant etc. — Arcadian Moon winery & brewery.

posts.title: Day 5 - Higginsville, MO

posts.content:
This morning we got on the road at 5 am to beat the afternoon gusts. We saw a travel trailer on its side from getting blown over! Headed through Nebraska today

It didn’t get windy until after noon.  Targeted a state park south of grand island.  Could be full- Stopped in Laramie for breakfast and gas.  

Arrived at the Mormon Island State rec area this afternoon . The temp is 100’degrees!!! 

It’s a pretty nice park with electricity. It’s also Jake Sotos home town. Our site is private enough with no people with loose dogs near us so we felt comfortable letting the ladies out on their leashes. Lots of interesting birds that we haven’t seen and we are in the middle of the Sandhill Crane migration area. They fly over our campsite in flocks - they sound just like pterodactyls. How do we know what pterodactyls sound like? From Jurassic park of course! 

Looks really windy tomorrow.  We may take a layover day if it looks dicey in the freeway.

posts.title: Day 4 - Grand Island, NE

posts.content:
Woke up at 655AM in Declo, ID- it’s cold - 37, 43, 37, 46 - that’s current conditions here.  Getting batteries for our indoor/outdoor thermometer today.  Got on the road at the crack of 9 am

Decided to stop in Rawlins, WY. Camping option are pretty limited - plus it’s early enough in the Spring that most federal and state campgrounds are still closed and RV parks are in winter mode meaning limited utility access. No Harvest Hosts in the area either.

Stayed at the Desert Rose rv park.. not too bad, but mostly because it was mostly empty and we could get away from the full time riff raff. 

I80 is closed to rvs under 30000pounds.  Boy the winds in eastern wy are no joke. Yesterday afternoon the freeway was closed to high profile vehicles under 35k lbs (like us) between Rawlins and Laramie.

posts.title: Day 3 - Rawlins, WY

posts.content:
Waking up early in preparation for some quality camping world time.  Juntura is a dumpy expensive rv park.  

We were at camping world for probably 3 hours or so- maybe more.  We ended up leaving at 2.  But they fixed the air conditioner- it was a firefly issue.  Meaning the fancy control panel wasn’t talking to the AC unit. 

Impressed with the service at camping world! While they were working we spent some quality time stumbling around Walmart. 

Felt sorry for poor Hazel and Alice - we had to put them in the tiny little bathroom while the ac was getting worked on

Drove to delco, ID.  Stayed at an rv park (village of trees).  It’s a big park and pretty nice.  We tentatively planned the rest of our stops to Owensboro.

posts.title: Day 2 - Delco, ID

posts.content:
Launched our first ever x-country trip on Wednesday March 18. Left after lunch and went as far as Juntura, OR where it was 81 degrees at 5 pm! 

Discovered our air conditioning does not work which you actually do need when traveling in a metal hot box with two kitties who can’t really go outside on their leashes in campgrounds with loose doggies afoot. 

The fan works but compressor will not kick on.  On auto fan everything just shuts off.  

There is a little RV park at the cafe which is a bit sad but to which we were happy to support.
